text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended sharply lower in a downward correction to last week's rally. August lost $4.50 to close at $320.50 per tonne, while October closed $1.40 lower at $315.30 per tonne. There were no fresh news to influence trading. As anticipated raw sugar futures in New York closed weaker near the lows amid steady speculative liquidation in front-month July. July gave up 11 points to close at 11.26 cents/lb, while October lost 10 points to close at 11.15 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 5 and 6 points. Traders said Friday's options expiry should speed liquidation of the July contract.

RUSSIA - At the end of May the Rossakhsvyokla Sugar Beet Producers Association said that sugar beet sowings were almost finished and that the total area would be slightly below last year's 1.10 million ha. However, the latest figures signal, that the drop in the area sown to beet may be larger than had been expected. Up to June 9 the total area sown was not more than 902,000 ha, 20 per cent less than had been sown at the same date last year. This calls into question the beet production target for 1997 of 22 million tonnes, up from 16 million tonnes in 1996. Based on an acreage of 965,000 ha a crop of 22 million tonnes would require a beet yield of 22.80 tonnes per ha, while the 1990/95 average was only 17.63 tonnes. This means, that the beet production target is out of reach and that the crop could be at around last year's level or even less. No reasons were given for the drop in acreage but earlier reports said that fuel shortages could cause a drop in sowings.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 99,280 tonnes, raw value, down from 105,211 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 639,764 tonnes against 681,963 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.380 million tonnes compared to 1.635 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/March 1996/97 were Mauritius with 271,983 tonnes raws against 332,907 tonnes, Guyana with 111,673 tonnes compared to 73,510 tonnes and Fiji with 79,900 tonnes against 85,180 tonnes.

Sugar exports in March 1997 amounted to 47,375 tonnes, unchanged from last year's 47,478 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in October/March 1996/97 up to 157,133 tonnes, down from 173,416 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 390,747 tonnes compared to 560,076 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Israel with 60,820 tonnes whites against 50,717 tonnes, Norway with 19,131 tonnes, down from 21,306 tonnes and Hong Kong with 14,959 tonnes compared to 10,136 tonnes.

CZECH REPUBLIC - Sugar exports in April 1997 amounted to 7,521 tonnes, raw value, up from 1,275 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative exports in September/April 1996/97 up to 54,022 tonnes, up on last year's 17,202 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 27,684 tonnes compared to 35,029 tonnes in 1994/95.

Imports in September/April 1996/97 amounted to 9,388 tonnes, down from 10,601 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 were 21,013 tonnes compared to 10,989 tonnes in 1994/95. Exports can be expected to remain high for the remainder of the crop year given the country's excellent sugar output of 663,000 tonnes attained in 1996.

PHILIPPINES - According to ISO figures sugar imports in September/December 1996 amounted to 98,143 tonnes, down from 287,055 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached the record high of 853,422 tonnes, up on 102,299 tonnes imported in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in calendar year 1996 were Thailand with 257,040 tonnes raws, Brazil with 186,442 tonnes and Thailand with 109,598 tonnes whites.

The European Union awarded 33,600 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 42.295 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on June 11. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to June 11 reached 2,219,225 tonnes, which compares to 2,320,198 tonnes last year.
